recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-5493; future CDA-to-FHIR identifier changes should be handled under later Structured Documents mapping issues rather than by restoring the obsolete Bundle.id wording.
issue_request: FHIR-5493 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 Structured Documents clarification for Composition. It asked to preserve the CDA comparison that Composition.identifier corresponds to ClinicalDocument.setId and add that ClinicalDocument.id goes in the document Bundle identity, with the relationship described as equivalent in function rather than literally identical.
initial_application: The issue was applied in svn revision 4622, represented by git commit 9728390581527fbfe248afbde3a47bac77d46b2f. That commit added the sentence saying Bundle.id was equivalent in function to ClinicalDocument.id, with a caveat that interconversion is a transform.
additional_context: Composition is active in source/fhir.ini and source/composition/composition-introduction.xml feeds the current build. Later Structured Documents work under FHIR-30766 changed the mapping target from Bundle.id to Bundle.identifier, and that later decision is already represented on the combined branch. Current source/documents.html also distinguishes Bundle.identifier as the document identifier from Composition.identifier as the composition identifier.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. The active source still conveys the FHIR-5493 clarification, but in the later corrected form: Composition.identifier maps to ClinicalDocument.setId and Bundle.identifier is equivalent to ClinicalDocument.id.

related_jiras.note: Superseded FHIR-5493's original Bundle.id wording with Bundle.identifier for ClinicalDocument.id and is already represented on the combined branch.
SDWG minutes discussed Composition.identifier cardinality and recorded the same ClinicalDocument.id to Bundle.identifier mapping context, but the actual mapping change proceeded under FHIR-30766.
